title: History of India & National Movement
description: Chronology, political/social change, ideas, institutions, personalities and the freedom struggle.
approach: Build timelines and cause–effect maps; classify PYQs by period and demand.

title: Indian & World Geography
description: Physical processes, regions, climate, resources, population, maps and economic geography.
approach: Pair conceptual reading with atlas work and diagram-based recall.

title: Indian Polity & Constitution
description: Constitutional provisions, institutions, rights, federal relations and legal developments.
approach: Read provisions with institutional function, exceptions and current legal context.

title: Governance-related static concepts
description: Institutional functioning, accountability, public services and governance concepts that overlap with polity.
approach: Use primary category once and add governance as a secondary tag when appropriate.

title: Economic & Social Development
description: Macroeconomic mechanisms, financial system, public finance, agriculture, inclusion and indicators.
approach: Learn mechanisms and link indicators to official releases; avoid memorising figures without a year.

title: Environment & Ecology
description: Ecology concepts, ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation instruments, pollution and climate change.
approach: Anchor facts in core concepts, maps, species status and current official materials.

title: General Science
description: Foundational scientific principles and practical applications in health, biology, chemistry and physics.
approach: Prioritise explainable concepts and applied uses instead of encyclopaedic detail.

title: Science & Technology
description: Emerging and applied technologies, scientific institutions and developments in public use.
approach: Understand what the technology does, its principle, application, limits and associated institution.

title: Current Affairs & Contemporary Developments
description: Current issues connected with the notified syllabus; cross-tags other subjects rather than replacing them.
approach: Tag the subject underneath a current-affairs link; do not count it as an additional primary topic.

title: Interdisciplinary / Mixed
description: Questions that genuinely require two or more domains and cannot be faithfully represented by one main category.
approach: Select one primary label plus secondary tags; only use Mixed if one primary label would be misleading.
